title: A matrix color change over a span starts every cell at the matrix's color
body:
`fill m #ffcc00` on a matrix makes one `Paint` for the whole matrix. `timeline::paint` starts its track at the matrix's own `fill`, which is white by default. While the paint runs, `Matrix::repaint_fill` sets every cell to the track's color. Over a span such as `1s to 2s`, a cell with its own fill, such as `cell { at 0 1; fill #228833; }`, jumps to the matrix's fill at 1s and then blends to the new color. `stroke` and `text-color` work the same way through `Matrix::repaint_stroke` and `Matrix::repaint_text`. At an instant the jump does not show.

A row had the same problem until commit 1579407. There `timeline::by_cell` gives each cell of a row its own track, which starts from the cell's own color.

## Proposal

A matrix-wide color action makes one track per cell, each starting from that cell's color. `Paint::cell` addresses only a row cell today, so it needs a way to name a matrix cell.
